item.research_question: How can noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials be synthesized with precise control over their composition and crystal structure, and what is the role of noble metals in their formation?
item.material_system: Noble metal-based high-entropy alloys (NM-HEAs) with compositions including Pt, Ir, Ru, Pd, Fe, Cu, Ni, and Co
item.processing_route: Spray drying technique combined with thermal decomposition-reduction (SD-TDR) method, with parameters including heating rate of 3°C/min, thermal decomposition temperature of 300°C, and cooling rate of 5° to 10°C/min
item.test_conditions: Methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) performance tested in an aqueous solution of 0.5 M H2SO4 and 0.5 M CH3OH
key_findings: The synthesized PtNiCoCuRuIr HEA-3DNF demonstrates exceptional MOR performance, with a mass activity of 2637 mA/mgPt
Noble metals (Pt, Ru, and Ir) play a crucial role in facilitating the reduction of Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe by generating highly reactive hydrogen atoms on their surfaces
The phase composition of NM-HEA-3DNF can be precisely controlled by adjusting the reduction temperature and Pt-to-Ru atomic ratio
A phase transition from Pt-based fcc structures to Ru-based hcp structures can be achieved within PtNiCoCuRu HEA-3DNF
The SD-TDR method allows for the synthesis of NM-HEA nanomaterials with a 3DNF structure and single-phase solid solution
item.mechanism: The noble metals (Pt, Ru, and Ir) facilitate the reduction of Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe by generating highly reactive hydrogen atoms on their surfaces, leading to the formation of single-phase solid solution alloys
item.future_work: Further research is needed to explore the applications of NM-HEA nanomaterials in various catalytic fields and to develop more efficient and targeted material design
quotes: Noble metal–based high-entropy alloys (NM-HEAs) are promising catalysts because of their diverse compositions and complex surface structures
The PtNiCoCuRuIr HEA-3DNF exhibits superior methanol oxidation reaction performance (2637 milliamperes per milligram Pt)

records.text: Paper card. Question: How can noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials be synthesized with precise control over their composition and crystal structure, and what is the role of noble metals in their formation?. System: Noble metal-based high-entropy alloys (NM-HEAs) with compositions including Pt, Ir, Ru, Pd, Fe, Cu, Ni, and Co. Processing: Spray drying technique combined with thermal decomposition-reduction (SD-TDR) method, with parameters including heating rate of 3°C/min, thermal decomposition temperature of 300°C, and cooling rate of 5° to 10°C/min. Test conditions: Methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) performance tested in an aqueous solution of 0.5 M H2SO4 and 0.5 M CH3OH. Findings: The synthesized PtNiCoCuRuIr HEA-3DNF demonstrates exceptional MOR performance, with a mass activity of 2637 mA/mgPt; Noble metals (Pt, Ru, and Ir) play a crucial role in facilitating the reduction of Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe by generating highly reactive hydrogen atoms on their surfaces; The phase composition of NM-HEA-3DNF can be precisely controlled by adjusting the reduction temperature and Pt-to-Ru atomic ratio; A phase transition from Pt-based fcc structures to Ru-based hcp structures can be achieved within PtNiCoCuRu HEA-3DNF; The SD-TDR method allows for the synthesis of NM-HEA nanomaterials with a 3DNF structure and single-phase solid solution. Mechanism: The noble metals (Pt, Ru, and Ir) facilitate the reduction of Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe by generating highly reactive hydrogen atoms on their surfaces, leading to the formation of single-phase solid solution alloys. Future work: Further research is needed to explore the applications of NM-HEA nanomaterials in various catalytic fields and to develop more efficient and targeted material design. Quote: "Noble metal–based high-entropy alloys (NM-HEAs) are promising catalysts because of their diverse compositions and complex surface structures"
